summary: This page from the German Embassy in the UK explains the German D-Visa for self-employed entrepreneurs and people starting a business in Germany. It covers visa-free entry rules for British and other listed citizens, the criteria assessed for self-employment residence permits, the required application documents, and where to apply. Processing may take several months to a year depending on the project's complexity.
one_line: German Embassy UK guide to the D-Visa for self-employed entrepreneurs and business start-ups, including eligibility criteria and application documents.
key_facts: The D-Visa for self-employed entrepreneurs is intended to make it easier for innovative people from abroad to start their own business in Germany and help create jobs.
British citizens may apply to the local immigration office (Ausländerbehörde) for residence permits after arriving in Germany without a prior visa.
Citizens of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, Korea (Republic) and the United States of America share the same visa-free privilege as British citizens.
Residents entering visa-free must register their new residence (Anmeldung) with the authorities within 2 weeks of moving in.
Visa-free entrants must apply for a residence permit at the local immigration office within the first 90 days of their stay.
Applicants may only pursue economic activities once issued a residence permit explicitly authorising such employment.
Approval depends on a positive assessment of business viability, entrepreneurial experience, capital investment, effects on employment and training, and contribution to innovation and research.
Applicants must be able to finance their business concept with their own capital or a loan, and there must be an economic interest in or regional demand for the product or service.
Applicants must submit a valid passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least six months, with at least 2 consecutive blank pages.
Applicants need 2 fully biometric passport photos measuring 35 x 45 mm.
Applicants must provide confirmation of health insurance cover commensurate with statutory German public health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung).
Processing in this visa category requires several months, even up to a year, depending on the complexity of the project.
Applicants must apply directly with the German Mission having jurisdiction for their place of residence; the German Missions in the UK operate from London and Edinburgh.
Accompanying spouses are generally not exempt from the basic German language proficiency requirement, though some exemptions apply.
